page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s3.medium is an x86_64 architecture virtual server provisioned through KVM virtualization. The instance features 4 dedicated virtual CPUs alongside 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an exact 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The instance configuration contains zero integrated graphics processing units and provides no onboard local disk storage, meaning boot environments and persistent filesystem data require external network-attached block storage volumes. Complimentary public IPv4 networking is also not included in the standard allocation.

The constrained memory footprint relative to its 4 dedicated execution cores creates a specific resource profile. Because total RAM is limited to 1.0 GB per vCPU, memory-intensive processes such as large relational databases or high-capacity in-memory caches are unsuitable. Instead, this resource density provides qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded tasks with modest working sets, preventing expenditure on unutilized RAM. Typical workloads matching this profile include distributed compute workers, lightweight continuous integration runners, stateless API processing, and batch jobs characterized by purely CPU-driven computational requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s3.medium is an x86_64 compute instance running under KVM virtualization. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The server includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local physical storage, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for system disks and stateful application data. Without complimentary public IPv4 connectivity, external routing must be provisioned separately. Given its low memory footprint relative to its core count, ecs.s3.medium operates cost-efficiently for strictly compute-driven workloads that require multi-threaded processing while consuming negligible memory. It is suitable for batch execution, CPU-focused worker nodes, stateless microservices, and lightweight compilation tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools or local NVMe storage.
